item.title: Lebanon appeals to Israel’s allies to stop strikes as death toll rises
item.summary: The Iran war is expanding into Lebanon, as the Israeli offensive to dismantle Hezbollah has displaced 800,000 people there, with more than 680 people killed.

item.title: U.S. sailors injured in fire aboard aircraft carrier supporting Iran war
item.summary: The incident, in a laundry room on the USS Gerald R. Ford, is another setback during the ship’s extended deployment.

item.title: Nations agree to release oil reserves as war in Iran hits global economy
item.summary: The International Energy Agency announced that it would carry out its largest-ever release of oil reserves — 400 million barrels.

item.title: Satellite companies restrict access to Middle East imagery amid Iran war
item.summary: The U.S.-based companies, Planet Labs and Vantor, say they were not instructed by any government to restrict image access.

item.title: Iranian school was on U.S. target list, may have been mistaken as military site
item.summary: The strike on an Iranian elementary school killed at least 175, many of them children, raising questions as to whether the military’s use of AI-enabled targeting was a factor.

item.title: After Iran assault, Russians say U.S. can’t be trusted in Ukraine talks
item.summary: As Washington focuses on its push to topple Iran’s government, delaying talks on Russia’s war in Ukraine, some in Moscow say the Kremlin must achieve its goals militarily.

item.title: As Israel targets Iran, Gaza’s nascent recovery stalls and Hamas gains strength
item.summary: Food deliveries and the prospect of medical care abroad gave Gazans reasons to hope, but the Iran conflict has closed the door on progress again.

item.title: UAE, an oasis for business and partying, faces war
item.summary: Iranian airstrikes have shaken Persian Gulf countries, undermining their reputations as havens of wealth and stability and forcing them to take sides in a war they opposed.

item.title: Pentagon says about 140 troops wounded, 8 severely, in war with Iran
item.summary: The vast majority of the wounded had minor injuries, a Pentagon spokesman said. The toll is higher than previously disclosed.

item.title: Ukraine strikes Russian electronics plant that builds missile components
item.summary: The general staff said that it used Storm Shadow missiles, which are produced jointly by Britain and France, to hit a plant that makes microchips and high-end electronics.
